rv.q: Therefore it’s no surprise that the combination of both in this splendid new production from Carrie Cracknell is intoxicating, bringing new shades of complexity to this famous, much-revived work about an affair gone badly wrong in the aftermath of the Second World War.
The National Theatre’s production of THE DEEP BLUE SEA is both captivating and atmospheric.
Absorbing though it is to watch, this version of 'The Deep Blue Sea' doesn't take us to those eerie and mysterious depths of love that I think Rattigan's play really had in mind.
Terence Rattigan’s 1952 play about the consequences of a failing, desperately sad love affair teems with life in a superbly realised, electrifying production at the National Theatre.
McCrory fills that set with Hester as few can ever have.
The results are mixed, with a lack of coherence more in evidence than cohesion.

cn.t: Helen McCrory delivers a powerful performance in this electrifying National revival of Rattigan's masterpiece, with critics praising Carrie Cracknel's superbly realized direction and the production's depth and emotional resonance.
